text:
mira: Hey team — quick design review request. Attached screenshots of the new capacity card where we let customers set min/max, burst, and pick a GPU pool. Questions: is a combined range slider + numeric inputs confusing? Do we need a separate “burst” toggle or inline burst stepper? Also worried about how we show SLO guardrail warnings when min > SLO recommended min. Screenshot: https://figma.redwood/flows/capacity-card (see comments) jon: Thanks Mira. My gut: range slider for quick adjustments + two small number inputs for fine-tuning is ok, but it needs clear affordances. Right now the slider thumb labels overlap at small ranges. If thumbs collide, switch to stacked numeric inputs and show a short tooltip: “Use numbers to set exact min/max.” :thinking_face: sam: Accessibility nit — sliders are notoriously awful for keyboard/screen reader. If we keep the slider, each thumb needs focusable handles and ARIA live updates. Prefer having dedicated `Min` and `Max` inputs first-class (tab order) and treat the slider as a visual helper only. Example aria pattern we can use: ```
\n \n \n \n \n
``` sam: Also ensure the slider has `aria-valuetext` reflecting both values when focused. alexa: Copy thought — instead of just “Burst”, use “Burst capacity (short-term)” and add a question-mark tooltip that explains billing and preemption behavior. Users keep asking whether burst consumes reserved capacity. Tooltip text suggestion: \"Burst capacity lets you exceed your reserved pool for brief periods. Usage above reserved capacity is billed at on-demand rates and may be preempted under contention.\" mira: Good — I like highlighting billing implications. For the SLO slider: should the guardrail be inline (red banner under controls) or modal on save? Currently the mock shows an inline banner: \"Warning: Selected min may violate 99th percentile latency SLO. Recommend min <= 12 GPUs.\" jon: Inline banner is less disruptive. Add an inline affordance: small link “Why this?” that opens the diagnostics panel on the right. Also suggest a subtle gradient or icon to indicate severity rather than full modal. sam: Accessibility check for color: use icon + text not color alone. Contrast needs to pass AA. For the banner background, check we keep contrast ratio >= 3:1 against body text per WCAG for non-text contrast. alexa: UX micro-copy: change “Set burst” CTA to “Enable burst capacity” and “Burst limit” label to “Burst max (GPUs)”. Also for the pool selector, replace “GPU pool” with “GPU pool (region)” when region matters. mira: Quick follow-ups: 1) Should we show an inline cost estimate next to numeric inputs? 2) Do we auto-correct when min > max input accidentally? Right now the mock clamps max to min and shows a toast. Thoughts? jon: I prefer inline validation with an error state on the offending input rather than a toast. Toasts are easy to miss. For auto-correction: do not auto-change someone’s values without explicit confirmation — instead highlight and explain. Maybe an inline checkbox: “Sync min and max to same value” after they set conflicting values. sam: Keyboard flows: when users increment with arrow keys on the number input, we should respect step sizes (1 GPU by default, but allow smaller decimals for vCPU-based pools). Also ensure increment buttons have accessible labels: `aria-label=\"increase min GPUs\"` etc. devex-bot: Figma comment created by mira on frame: Capacity card / Iteration-B. Link: https://figma.redwood/iter/CapacityCardB. mira: Great commentary — I'll update the mock with: stacked numeric inputs visible on small ranges, slider as visual-only when thumbs collide, aria patterns from Sam, copy updates from Alexa, inline banner with “Why this?” link and cost estimate mock next to inputs. Will post updated frames tomorrow. Thanks! :raised_hands: jon: One last thing — in the GPU pool picker, can we add a small latency icon + numeric p50/p99 hovercard so customers can make informed choices? It would pair nicely with the SLO guardrail. alexa: Love that. Add a small “i” icon and tooltip: “typical latency • p50 / p99”. mira: Adding to the spec. I'll also add acceptance criteria: keyboard-only must be able to set min/max and toggle burst, banner must have link to diagnostics, and error states must be explicit (no silent clamping). sam: Thanks — once you push the updated frames ping me and I’ll run the a11y sweep. mira: Will do.
